info.text:
Bankruptcy wipes out all your debt? Not even close.
US bankruptcy filings hit 621,111 in the 12 months ending Sept 30, 2026, up 11.4% from a year earlier and the fourth straight yearly rise (US Courts).
A discharge can wipe out debts like credit cards and medical bills.
Under 11 U.S.C. 523, child support, alimony, recent taxes, criminal fines, fraud debts (usually) and drunk-driving injury debts generally survive. Student loans survive unless you prove undue hardship.
Since Nov 2022, a DOJ and Education Dept attestation process has applied to federal student loan hardship cases.
Sources: US Courts (Bankruptcy Basics, Table F); 11 U.S.C. 523; DOJ guidance, Nov 17, 2022.
News and education, not financial advice.
